title: Jo. Antonio Bilia to Francesco II Sforza, Duke of Milan, Burgos, 22 November 1527 (BnF fr. 3013 no. 43, ff. 102r-v; catalogue item 291, part)

documents.shelfmark: BnF Français 3013 no. 43, ff. 102r-v (Gallica btv1b9060138r views 164, 165, 167)
documents.route: Burgos -> Francesco II Sforza, Duke of Milan

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the letter or elsewhere in fr. 3013, and none found in print (contributor's search: CSP Spain iii/2, CSP Venice iv, L&P iv); Cerioni 1970 and Giudici 2018 not checked.

transcription.source: Gallica / BnF IIIF full-size images of a microfilm (views 164, 165)
transcription.notes: Contributed by Harumi-Matsuba (issue #55): Claude Opus 5.5 transcription, three independent OpenAI Codex transcriptions, two rounds of AI image checks (12 corrections on f. 102r). No human check. Measured: f. 102r 505 signs (contributed/data/transcription_f102r.txt), f. 102v 118 signs (transcription_f102v_unconfirmed.txt), 623 in all. Spot-checked here on view 164: lines 1-5, 81 signs, all names agree, three second digits indistinguishable.

system.summary: Sforza chancery cipher of the Cavaliere Bilia (DECODE R5258): barred base letters with two-digit numbers for syllables in ordered rows, bare numbers and signs for letters with homophones, a few word codes, a nomenclator of names, and nulls.

diacritics.note: a two-digit number written over a barred base letter (G, B, D, o, H, R) selects the syllable

system.sibling_key: DECODE R5258 (ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1591 no. 24, 'Cum equite Bilie / extracta ex cifris'), the same key that reads Gilino's letter R8572 (targets/gilino1527); R5237 (cart. 1591 no. 3, 'Cum Egr[egi]o Bilia') is a numeric alphabet that does not fit.
system.notes: Syllable rows are in alphabetical order inside each base letter (B.31-50 ba..gu, D.51-65 la..nu, G.56-80 pa..tu, o.33-47 va..zu); the letter alphabet is not. Five signs used here are not on the sheet transcription (ß r, £ l, F c, tt t, qx ss), valued by the contributor from context. No. 42 of the same volume (to the ambassador Taverna, same date) is in a different cipher and is not part of this target.

prior_solution.where: No reading found: the contributor searched CSP Spain iii/2, CSP Venice iv, L&P iv, Cryptiana, this repository and GitHub (contributed/docs/PRIOR_CHECK.en.md, 20 Oct 2026); Cerioni 1970 and Giudici 2018 were not seen by them or here. The key R5258 was already transcribed in this repository (targets/gilino1527) and recovered independently by George Lasry; the contributor used both.

conditions.human_role: Contributed result: by the contributor's account a person chose the target and decided to publish; transcription, key table, decoding and checks were done by Claude (Opus 5.5, Sonnet) and OpenAI Codex, with no human check of the transcription. Project side: Daniel Bourdeau asked for the issue to be incorporated; Claude re-applied the project's key, re-scored and spot-checked the images.

solution.what: Contributor (Harumi-Matsuba, issue #55) matched BnF fr. 3013 no. 43 to the Sforza key DECODE R5258 ('Cum equite Bilie'), taking its values from this project's sheet transcription (targets/gilino1527) and George Lasry's recovery; R5237 tried and did not fit; no. 42 found to be in another cipher.

Contributor: Claude Opus 5.5 transcribed ff. 102r-v by sign name from the full-size images (505 + 118 signs); three blind OpenAI Codex transcriptions; disagreements judged by Codex and Claude Sonnet on line images in two rounds, 12 corrections on f. 102r where both agreed, 8 places left split.
Contributor: values for five signs absent from the sheet transcription inferred from context (ß r, £ l, F c, tt t, qx ss; 41 signs, 8.1% of f. 102r).

Contributor: f. 102r read with R5258: Bilia dined with an old lord (name code B.58) who complained of the Duke's treatment of 'conte Theophimo(?)'; Bilia urges a letter of guarantee. f. 102v left unconfirmed.

Contributor: 1000 key shuffles with a wordfreq Italian trigram score: 0 at or above the real key on f. 102r (also without the inferred signs); on f. 102v 24/1000 with sheet values only. Codex value agreement 94.9% (f. 102r), 82.2-83.1% (f. 102v).

Project: applied its own R5258 key files (targets/gilino1527) to the contributed transcription of f. 102r (decode_check.py): 459/505 signs valued, 440/459 (95.9%) agree with the contributor's values; it-cinquecento order 5 -2.183/char, best of 1000 shuffles -3.113, 0 at or above.

Project: checked the disputed signs on the R5258 sheet image (DECODE PDF): the crossed x is in the s column and the θ-like sign in the o column, as the contributor read them (our Gilino key had them as null and a); the nomenclator has no B.58.
Project: spot-checked f. 102r lines 1-5 (81 signs) against view 164 at full resolution: all sign names agree; three second digits (B.39/33 twice, G.69/65) cannot be told apart at this resolution.
Project: f. 102v decoded with the project's key: 102/118 signs valued, 94/102 agree with the contributor; LM -2.597 vs best shuffle -2.750: some words, no continuous sense; left unconfirmed.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): Harumi-Matsuba's transcriptions of ff. 102r-v, reading and decoded text of f. 102r and key (contributed/), and this project's own decodes of both pages as separate files; no contributor reading of f. 102v exists (they withheld it as unconfirmed)

Reading audit, per-document pass (George Lasry's sentence test): decoded_ours_f102v.txt read; no continuous sense in any of its seven lines. The f. 102v entry relabelled decoded, not read; class and fraction_read unchanged (504/623 already counted f. 102v as unread).

texts.label: f. 102r (30 cipher lines)
texts.summary: Bilia dined with an old lord (name code B.58) who complained that, by letters from his son-in-law, the Duke was troubling conte Theophimo(?) over earlier prohibitions; Bilia calmed him and advises the Duke to write a letter showing in deed the good will promised in words. Harumi-Matsuba's reading (contributed/) and this project's independent decode with its own R5258 key (decoded_ours_f102r.txt) are given separately.

texts.label: f. 102v (7 cipher lines, then clear close, Burgos 22 Nov 1527)
texts.summary: Seven cipher lines continuing the letter, then the clear close dated Burgos 22 November 1527, a clear postscript on the Emperor's journey to Valencia for Christmas, and Bilia's signature. The contributor gave no reading of the cipher lines; this project's decode gives words but no continuous sense.
texts.note: Raw decoder output for the seven cipher lines of f. 102v: bracketed unknown signs in every line and letter-level nonsense ("isoizde", "axaroaltn"); no continuous sense (reading audit, 22 Oct 2026); fix: a human sign-by-sign re-transcription of f. 102v. The clear close is described in the summary but is not part of this decryption.

outcome.method_basis: The key DECODE R5258 is docketed 'Cum equite Bilie', the Sforza chancery's key for this correspondent; the contributor applied it to the letter, and the project re-applied its own transcription of the sheet.
outcome.fraction_read_source: contributed/data/decoded_f102r.txt and the two transcriptions: 504 of 505 signs of f. 102r given a value (incl. nulls), 0 of 118 on f. 102v (unconfirmed) -> 504/623 cipher tokens.

gaps.detail: contributor's reading unconfirmed and not given; our key gives some words but no continuous sense; needs a human sign-by-sign re-transcription
